findings.reason: dn_route_rx_long() (remote receive of ETH_P_DNA_RT frames via dn_route_rcv) saves ptr = skb->data at line 550 before calling pskb_may_pull(skb, 21) at 552. For a non-linear skb (payload in frags), pskb_may_pull->__pskb_pull_tail can allocate a new head and free the old one, so the saved ptr dangles; the caller then reads attacker-influenced header bytes through it at 560-574 (cb->dst = dn_eth2dn(ptr), memcmp(ptr, dn_hiord_addr, 4), cb->src, cb->hops = *ptr++). Counterevidence checked: nothing re-derives ptr after the pull, and skb_pull(20) at 555 only advances data. Requires CONFIG_DECNET and a frag-backed skb so reallocation actually happens; no KASAN/reproducer run.
findings.conclusion: dn_route_rx_long() keeps ptr=skb->data across pskb_may_pull(skb,21), which can free the old head for a non-linear DNA_RT packet, so the later cb->dst/src/hops reads at 560-574 are a remote slab-use-after-free read (medium confidence).

findings.reason: dn_route_rx_short() saves ptr = skb->data at line 590, then pskb_may_pull(skb, 6) at 592 may reallocate/free the head on a non-linear skb; the stale ptr is dereferenced afterwards at 598-602 (cb->dst = *(__le16 *)ptr, cb->src, cb->hops = *ptr & 0x3f). Same remote ETH_P_DNA_RT receive path and same preconditions (CONFIG_DECNET, payload bytes in frags) as the long-header variant; no re-derivation of ptr exists.
findings.conclusion: dn_route_rx_short() captures ptr=skb->data before pskb_may_pull(skb,6) and reads cb->dst/src/hops through the stale pointer at 598-602, a remote slab-use-after-free read for short-header DNA_RT packets (medium confidence).

findings.reason: dn_nsp_rx_packet(), the NSP classification function reached after DECnet routing (dn_route_rx_packet), saves ptr = (unsigned char *)skb->data at line 722, then calls pskb_may_pull(skb, 2) at 725, pskb_may_pull(skb, 3) at 755, and pskb_may_pull(skb, 5) at 768; each can free/move the head for a non-linear skb. The stale ptr is dereferenced after the pulls at 729 (cb->nsp_flags = *ptr++), 761 (cb->dst_port = *(__le16 *)ptr) and 769 (cb->src_port = *(__le16 *)ptr). Counterevidence checked: nothing re-reads skb->data between the pulls and uses; skb_reset_transport_header only sets an offset. Requires CONFIG_DECNET and a frag-backed NSP frame.
findings.conclusion: dn_nsp_rx_packet() saves ptr=skb->data at 722, then pskb_may_pull(skb,2/3/5) at 725/755/768 can free the head and the stale ptr is read at 729/761/769 for nsp_flags/dst_port/src_port, a remote slab-use-after-free read in NSP classification (medium confidence).

findings.reason: ieee80211_rx_h_data() in the mac80211 RX pipeline saves tf = (void *)rx->skb->data at line 2558 (after the ethhdr h_proto check at 2556 confirmed the attacker-chosen ETH_P_TDLS ethertype), then calls pskb_may_pull(rx->skb, offsetof(...,u)) at 2560 inside the same condition; on a non-linear (A-MSDU/frag-backed) frame this pull can allocate a new head and free the old one, and the subsequent tf->payload_type / tf->category / tf->action_code reads at 2562-2565 use the stale pointer. Counterevidence checked: tf is not re-derived, and the short-circuit && means the reads happen only when the pull succeeded (i.e. exactly when reallocation was possible). Requires a WiFi driver delivering non-linear RX frames to the data handler.
findings.conclusion: ieee80211_rx_h_data() keeps tf=rx->skb->data across pskb_may_pull() at rx.c:2560 and dereferences tf->payload_type/category/action_code at 2562-2565, a stale-pointer slab-use-after-free read on non-linear TDLS WiFi RX frames (medium confidence).

candidates.reason: ip_forward() re-derives iph = ip_hdr(skb) at line 132 strictly AFTER skb_cow(skb, ...) at 130, and all later uses (ip_decrease_ttl(iph), rt_tos2priority(iph->tos)) happen after the re-derivation; this is the correct pattern, not the invariant violation.
candidates.conclusion: ip_forward.c is the safe reference pattern: the header pointer is taken after skb_cow, so no stale dereference.

candidates.reason: ip_forward_finish() calls ip_forward_options(skb) at line 72 with opt = &(IPCB(skb)->opt) taken at line 66; IPCB lives in skb->cb (not the head) so the caller-side read is not itself head-derived, but ip_forward_options() (net/ipv4/ip_options.c) manipulates the on-packet SRR option via header pointers and may itself hold stale head pointers across pskb operations; this callee body was not read to a conclusion in this session.
candidates.conclusion: Follow up: read net/ipv4/ip_options.c ip_forward_options() to check whether any header pointer it derives from the skb head survives an internal pskb_may_pull/pskb_pull and is dereferenced afterwards on the forwarded-SRR path.

coverage_gaps: The two-level caller expansion of every pskb_may_pull/pskb_pull/skb_cow/pskb_expand_head/NF_HOOK call site in net/ and drivers/net/ was not completed; the session's greps were triaged down to the DECnet, mac80211, ip_forward and NCSI/L2CAP sets before the finalize order.

Per-protocol skb control-block structs (any *_skb_cb with pointer- or offset-typed fields, beyond DN_SKB_CB and IPCB) were not systematically enumerated and their cb-stored values not traced across helpers that can move the head.

Non-linearity preconditions were assessed structurally (which subsystems linearize before parsing) without a per-driver audit of which RX paths actually deliver frag-backed skbs to the DECnet and mac80211 handlers reported here.

No runtime KASAN build, reproducer, or compilation was performed against the read-only snapshot, so head reallocation on each reported path is inferred from the __pskb_pull_tail reallocation logic rather than observed.
limitations: All four findings are source-reading hypotheses: triggering requires a non-linear skb so __pskb_pull_tail actually reallocates and frees the old head, and CONFIG_DECNET=y/m for the three DECnet sites, so exploitability may be narrower than the seed's phonet case.

net/phonet/pep.c pep_get_sb was excluded by instruction and never considered as a report target; line numbers are valid only for the supplied s02 tree (snapshot revision opaque, no git history or network used).

The mac80211 finding's stale reads occur inside the same boolean expression as the pull, so a compiler could in principle reorder the loads; the vulnerability judgment rests on C evaluation-order semantics (pull first due to &&) and source reading, not on generated code.
